status: Open — build-boundary fast repair applied; size and startup blocker remains
area: Onefile release packaging / startup budget / release build boundary
finding: The frozen onefile release currently violates its enforced artifact and startup budget. The separately reproducible package-script boundary drift was repaired, but the remaining budget failures still block release-quality acceptance even when root-drop validation succeeds.
expectedBehavior: A release candidate must keep the onefile artifact within its declared size and cold/warm startup budgets, and the package build script must invoke scripts/build-onefile-release.ts so the build boundary remains reviewable and deterministic.
evidenceOrRepro: Before the fast repair, node --strip-types scripts/validate-onefile-budget.ts reported ONEFILE_BUILD_SCRIPT_BOUNDARY_DRIFT because build:onefile-release invoked scripts/run-sealed-runner-build.ts onefile rather than the canonical TypeScript builder. After restoring node --strip-types scripts/build-onefile-release.ts, the same real validator no longer reported boundary drift but still failed honestly: onefile size 5,965,623 / 4,500,000 bytes, cold startup 4,717.99ms / 4,000ms, and warm startup 2,548.25ms / 2,500ms. The same runner-sync build passed scripts/validate-root-drop-release.ts, so this is isolated to the onefile release surface rather than a general runner-sync failure. Largest reported payloads include packages/cli/dist/commands/tasks/legacy/implementation.js (147,588 bytes) and docs/governance/error-code-registry.json (134,476 bytes).
containment: Do not publish a release candidate as onefile-budget compliant while this validator fails. Keep the current validated root-drop artifact intact; do not loosen size or timing budgets merely to make the gate green.
followUp: The canonical package-script boundary was restored on 2026-09-05: build:onefile-release now invokes node --strip-types scripts/build-onefile-release.ts, so ONEFILE_BUILD_SCRIPT_BOUNDARY_DRIFT is no longer expected. The size and cold/warm failures remain open and must not be masked. Next perform a bounded onefile composition inventory: identify non-runtime payloads and duplicate/legacy command closures, add regression evidence for size and cold/warm startup, then rebuild and rerun validate-onefile-budget.ts.
